rules.statement: After a successful interactive sign-in, redirect only to a `ReturnUrl` that has been validated as a local URL (for example with `Url.IsLocalUrl` or `LocalRedirect`), never to an unvalidated caller-supplied URL.
rules.why: The ADR requires the login endpoint to return to a validated local ReturnUrl after issuing the cookie, which prevents open-redirect attacks.
rules.check: Look for login/sign-in handlers that call `Redirect(returnUrl)` or set a Location header from a query/form value without a local-URL check.

rules.statement: An interactive login endpoint must verify credentials through the existing local-account credential store used by the other grants, and must not add a second credential verifier.
rules.why: Reusing the one local-account store keeps a single credential path, so login adds no new authentication model, credential store or persistence.
rules.check: Look for new password hashing/verification logic or new user/credential stores in login UI code instead of calls to the existing local-account authentication services.

rules.statement: An interactive login/consent UI must plug into the existing ASP.NET Core authentication scheme seam (register a scheme whose name matches the configured challenge/authenticate scheme and set its `LoginPath`) rather than changing the authorize/authenticate/challenge pipeline.
rules.why: The UI is only the form surface, not a new authentication model; the server-driven cookie challenge flow stays unchanged.
rules.check: Look for UI changes that modify the authorization endpoint's authenticate/challenge handlers or bypass `ChallengeAsync`/`AuthenticateAsync`, instead of adding a cookie scheme and its login path.

rules.statement: Form elements that browser automation depends on must have their stable ids (e.g. `username`, `password`, `login`, `consent-allow`, `consent-deny`) set explicitly, defined in one place, and must never rely on framework-generated ids such as Material UI's.
rules.why: The stable-locator contract is the architectural invariant for conformance automation; changing an id without updating the automation config silently breaks it.
rules.check: Look for login/consent markup or components where these ids are missing, renamed, generated automatically, or duplicated across files without updating the automation `browser` config.

rules.statement: A dev- or conformance-grade login/consent module must only be enabled by an explicit opt-in registration method and must never be wired by default in library service registration.
rules.why: The module is not a production login experience; it is enabled only under the conformance profile.
rules.check: Look for the dev interactive authentication registration being called from default `Add*` extension methods or unconditionally in production host setup.
